sections.title: Identification and habitat
sections.text: The catalogue entry and its plate represent Lamium album, white dead-nettle, rather than the whole genus Lamium. This rhizomatous perennial grows to about 60 cm and occurs in hedges, woodland edges and disturbed ground in Europe and Asia.

sections.title: Leaves and flowers
sections.text: The stems are square and bear opposite, toothed leaves. Unlike stinging nettles, white dead-nettle has no stinging hairs. Its white, two-lipped flowers cluster at the stem nodes and produce four small nutlets.

sections.title: Edibility
sections.text: Young leaves and flowers are eaten raw; older leaves can be cooked. Identification must be certain before gathering any wild plant.
